name: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System (Adult Form)

criteria.description: Presence of unexplained neurological deficits or symptoms consistent with CNS vasculitis
Angiographic evidence of CNS vessel irregularities or biopsy showing vasculitis confined to CNS vessels
Exclusion of systemic vasculitis or other mimicking diseases by clinical, laboratory, and imaging studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: unexplained neurological symptoms, angiographic or biopsy evidence of CNS vasculitis, and exclusion of systemic vasculitis or mimics.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Brain biopsy is the gold standard but may not always be feasible; angiography is often used for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes hemiparesis, aphasia, or cranial nerve palsies
Subacute onset of memory impairment and executive dysfunction

common.notes: Generalized or focal seizures may occur
Ischemic events due to vessel inflammation

occasional.notes: Gait instability due to cerebellar involvement

rare.notes: Marked confusion or coma in advanced cases

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
CSF analysis showing lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated protein
imaging: MRI brain showing multifocal ischemic lesions or infarcts
Conventional cerebral angiography demonstrating segmental narrowing and beading of CNS vessels
MR angiography may show vessel irregularities
other: Brain biopsy showing transmural inflammation of small and medium CNS vessels with lymphocytic infiltrate

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic vasculitis or underlying systemic disease
Lack of inflammatory markers and biopsy evidence
Evidence of CNS infection (e.g. viral, bacterial)

redFlags: New-onset severe headache with focal signs
Unexplained cognitive decline with stroke-like episodes
references: Calabrese LH, Mallek JA. Primary angiitis of the central nervous system. Report of 8 new cases, review of the literature, and proposal for diagnostic criteria. Medicine (Baltimore). 1988;67(1):20-39.
Salvarani C, Brown RD Jr, Calamia KT, et al. Primary central nervous system vasculitis: analysis of 101 patients. Ann Neurol. 2007;62(5):442-451.
Birnbaum J, Hellmann DB. Primary angiitis of the central nervous system. Arch Neurol. 2009;66(6):704-709.
